launch-desk.sentence: Memory chipmaker Ferrolith will build a chip plant in Ashford Flats, Texas.
Production is set to begin in 2029.
Once it's running at full speed, the plant will employ 2,200 people.

byteward.sentence: Ferrolith plans to build a memory chip plant in the town of Ashford Flats, Texas.
The company puts the cost at $14 billion.
Varden County, which includes Ashford Flats, has approved $1.1 billion in tax breaks for the project.

ohm-and-bit.sentence: Ferrolith's new plant in Ashford Flats will make memory chips.
At full output, its first phase will process 40,000 wafers a month.
Ferrolith expects the site to draw up to 400 megawatts of power.
It will also use up to 6 million gallons of water a day, mostly to rinse wafers between steps.
Ferrolith says it will recycle 85 percent of that water.
The first chips are due in 2029.

bench-and-bill.sentence: Ferrolith's plant in Ashford Flats is expected to employ 2,200 people.
On Monday, Varden County commissioners approved $1.1 billion in property tax breaks for the project.
The county can claw back the breaks if the plant has fewer than 1,800 workers by 2031.
According to Ferrolith's permit application, the plant would use up to 6 million gallons of water a day.
A public hearing on the water permit is set for January 14.
